reason: The passage presents Moses's leadership model in response to the Israelites' fear and complaints as one of reassurance, faith, and divine guidance—not violence. When the people express fear and doubt ('Why have you brought us out to die in the wilderness?'), Moses responds with 'Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today' and 'The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still.' The violence in the text (the drowning of Egyptian forces) is divine judgment against external enemies, not a leadership tool wielded by Moses against his own people. The passage emphasizes obedience to God's instructions and trust in divine providence as the model for good leadership, not coercion or violence towards the community.
